The computer lab was empty except for Parul, who sat with her phone face-down and her bag clutched on her lap. Harish, the computer teacher, was locking the cupboards when he heard a small sound. "Parul? Is something wrong?"
She turned the phone over. Someone she had never met was threatening to share her private photos unless she sent more and paid. "I can't tell my parents," she whispered.
Harish stayed calm. "You did nothing wrong. The shame belongs to the person threatening you. Don't reply, don't pay. We'll save the screenshots, call your parents together, and report it to the cybercrime helpline."
Parul's shoulders shook as she nodded. Harish stayed in the lab until her mother arrived.

qa.q: Where was Parul when Harish found her?
qa.a: She was in the empty computer lab.

qa.q: Why did Parul whisper that she can't tell her parents?
qa.a: She seems frightened and ashamed and worried about how they will react, though the person making the threat is the one in the wrong.
He said not to reply or pay, to save the screenshots, to call her parents together and to report it to the cybercrime helpline.

qa.q: How might Parul's mother feel when she arrives?
qa.a: She may feel shock and worry for her daughter, and hopefully relief that Parul is safe and no longer facing it alone.

grounding: Shows a teen threatened over private photos and a teacher responding with no compliance, evidence, adults and reporting.

Nirmala: dolma are u there. i need help
Dolma: what happened
Nirmala: someone i met in a game did a video call last week. he took screenshots
Nirmala: now he says if i don't send more pictures he'll send them to everyone in my school. he found my class list
Dolma: nirmala this is not your fault
Nirmala: i feel so ashamed. i want to disappear
Dolma: don't send anything. don't reply to him anymore. don't pay if he asks
Dolma: screenshot everything he said. his name, his messages, all of it
Nirmala: ok. done
Dolma: now we tell ur mom. right now. i'm coming over, 5 minutes
Nirmala: she'll be so angry
Dolma: she'll be angry at HIM. this is a crime. the shame is his, not yours

Twenty minutes later, Nirmala's mother read the screenshots with both girls beside her. She held Nirmala's hand. "You did right to tell me." She called the cybercrime helpline, then filed a report on the national cybercrime website before dinner.

qa.q: What did the man threaten to do if Nirmala didn't send more pictures?
qa.a: He said he would send them to everyone in her school.

qa.q: What was Nirmala feeling after the threat?
qa.a: Nirmala felt deeply ashamed and frightened, saying she wanted to disappear.

qa.q: Which steps did Dolma urge, and why are they right?
qa.a: Dolma urged Nirmala not to send anything, stop replying, not pay, save evidence and tell her mother now, which cuts off the blackmailer and gets adult help.

qa.q: How did Nirmala's mother respond, and why did it matter?
qa.a: She held Nirmala's hand, said she did right to tell, and called the helpline and filed a report before dinner, showing Nirmala she was not to blame.

grounding: It shows a teen threatened with the sharing of her photos unless she sends more, who stops replying, saves evidence, tells an adult who reports it, and learns the shame belongs to the offender.

passage:
In Hoshiarpur, Jyoti had stopped eating properly for three days. Her Shalini Mausi, visiting from Ludhiana, noticed at once.

On Wednesday evening, Mausi sat beside her on the charpai on the terrace. "Something is wrong, puttar. You can tell me."

Jyoti's voice came out in pieces. A boy she'd met online had saved photos she'd shared of herself. Now he was saying that if she didn't send more, and some money, he'd post them and tag her father.

"I'm so ashamed," she whispered. "It's my fault for sending anything."

Mausi held her face in both hands. "Listen to me. It is not your fault. What he's doing is a crime. The shame is his."

She asked Jyoti not to reply to him again, and not to send anything or pay anything. Together they took screenshots of every message and his profile. Then Mausi went downstairs with Jyoti and told her parents.

That night her father called the cybercrime helpline, and the next morning they went together to the police station's cyber cell.

qa.q: Where was Shalini Mausi visiting from?
qa.a: Shalini Mausi was visiting from Ludhiana.

qa.q: What was Jyoti feeling when she told Mausi?
qa.a: Jyoti felt deeply ashamed and afraid, blaming herself for having sent anything.

qa.q: What steps did Mausi take that protected Jyoti?
qa.a: Mausi told her not to reply, send or pay, saved screenshots of the messages and profile, and told her parents that same evening.

qa.q: Why did Mausi say the shame belonged to him?
qa.a: Mausi wanted Jyoti to see that threatening someone with photos is a crime, so the blame lies with the offender, not with Jyoti.

grounding: It shows a teen threatened with sharing of her photos unless she sends more and pays, who stops replying, saves evidence and tells adults who report it, learning the shame belongs to him.
